Subject: sudden response-time drift — seeing tail in production

Hi Vivek / team,

We started seeing a shift in our 95th/99th percentile response times around 13:40 PDT. The impact is intermittent — not all requests, but enough that our checkout abandonment went up. Sample from our side: p95 from ~220ms -> ~1.1s, p99 spikes to 3.2s. No obvious change on our app tier.

Can Redwood confirm whether there was any rollout, config change, or infra maintenance in us-west-2 around that time? We have a production canary running; attaching the canary export.

– Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden response-time drift — seeing tail in production

Quick update from infra traces: around 13:39 PDT we see a short burst of KV cache evictions for BrightCart's shard across two nodes. Eviction rate jumped ~7x for ~8 minutes, coincident with the p95 jump in the canary. No full restart or rolling upgrade logged. I pulled kernel selection logs — a small adjustment to kernel scheduling was merged to canary earlier today (INF-4219) but the routing table shows no deliberate rollout to BrightCart's dedicated capacity.

Hypothesis: transient memory pressure on two GPU hosts caused a cascade of KV cache misses which increased token recomputation time for long-context requests. This manifests as tail latency spikes.

Immediate mitigation options: 
- Backfill evicted KV from a recent KV snapshot (fast but manual).
- Temporarily route BrightCart traffic to a sibling variant with a higher cache-residency profile (costly but reduces tail).
- Throttle long-context requests at the edge for 15 minutes while we stabilize (customer-visible).

I recommend routing to sibling variant + continuing root cause analysis.

Ben

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 4 Jul 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden response-time drift — triage, product asks, and customer readout

Status update and engineering asks: 

What we found (summary):
- Root cause appears to be transient memory pressure on two hosts in the BrightCart shard; eviction propagated because their tenant had high fanout requests that stressed KV residency. No change in model weights or quantization.
- Kernel scheduling tweak (INF-4219) touched canary but did not target BrightCart; unrelated but noted.

Short-term mitigations completed: 
- Traffic routed to protective variant (done at 08:45 PDT). Canary metrics show p95 back to baseline within ~6 minutes. (see p95_response_trend.png)
- SRE temporarily increased TTL for KV snapshots to reduce chances of re-eviction (rolling config applied).

Product / Roadmap asks (for prioritization):
1) Make a controlled rollback guard for kernel scheduling merges — preventing accidental canary bleed-through into dedicated pools. Owner: Product + Runtime.
2) Add per-tenant KV residency alerts tied to eviction-rate thresholds (SRE + Observability).
3) Evaluate an automated fallback variant routing policy for sustained eviction spikes (Product + Runtime).

Customer messaging: we sent the short readout per Alex's ask and routed traffic. Next steps: formal post-incident RCA and timeline for any mitigations that require infra changes.

Action items (owners):
- Diego: complete detailed trace upload and attach to JIRA INF-4219 (done).
- Ben: run a soak job on the two hosts to identify memory leak/vector (ETA 24h).
- Marissa: draft RCA and product/prioritization brief for next-week roadmap sync.
- Vivek: coordinate with Sales/CS for any credits or SLA exceptions if BrightCart requests.

Grace — flagging for potential executive summary if this needs leadership escalation.

Diego
